verdict.rationale: Both changes make the loader strict, collect every problem, reject unknown keys and exit with status 78 and a clean message, so they are close in substance. B keeps closer to the documented contract: it leaves `0s` accepted and says so openly instead of inventing a new rule. B's tests also cover boundaries, empty-but-present values and a blank token. A's report wrongly claims a missing `upstream.url` used to crash with a NullPointerException, when the old `catch (Exception e)` actually turned it into a null URI. A's one real edge is case-insensitive booleans, which keeps old values like `TRUE` working.
a_issues: Rejects `request.timeout=0s`, a rule the README does not state and the task did not ask for.
Report claims a missing `upstream.url` used to throw a NullPointerException; the old code caught it and returned a null URI.
No tests that each number is accepted at its exact minimum, or that a key present with an empty value is rejected.
b_issues: `metrics.enabled` now only accepts lowercase `true`/`false`, so a config that used `TRUE` (accepted by the old `Boolean.parseBoolean`) will now fail to start.
The URL scheme check is case-sensitive, so `HTTPS://...` is rejected.
Adds a `ConfigException(message, cause)` constructor, a small extra beyond what was needed.

verdict.rationale: Both changes make the loader strict in nearly the same way: they collect all problems, reject unknown keys, exit with status 78 and print a clean message from Main. A stays closer to the documented contract and flags the zero-timeout question for the developer, where B adds an undocumented rule that rejects zero timeouts. A also tests each numeric minimum boundary. B's report wrongly says a missing upstream.url used to crash with a NullPointerException, but the old code caught that exception and returned null.
a_issues: metrics.enabled now accepts only lowercase true/false, so an existing config using `True` or `TRUE` now fails to start, although Boolean.parseBoolean used to accept it.
The list of known keys is repeated in every unknown-key error line, which makes the message noisy when several keys are wrong.
b_issues: Rejects `request.timeout=0s`, a rule the README does not state and that was not requested; the README table was not updated to say the timeout must be greater than zero.
The report wrongly says a missing upstream.url used to crash with a NullPointerException; the old uri() caught the exception and returned null.
Only the zero-retries boundary is tested; acceptance of worker.threads and queue.capacity at 1 is not.
No test covers a present-but-empty optional value or a blank api.token.
